name: Productive
tagline: All-in-one agency management: projects, time tracking, budgets, resource planning, invoicing and profitability reporting.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Productive is not one feature, it is a stack of them: time tracking, project budgets, resource scheduling, invoicing, expenses and margin reporting, all wired to the same numbers. If you are a solo freelancer or a two-person shop, the part you actually use is small: log hours against a project, compare to budget, send an invoice, see whether the work made money. That is a very buildable weekend app with SQLite and a couple of tables, and honestly it will fit your billing quirks better than a generic agency tool. What you cannot one-shot is the part that makes it worth per-seat money at scale: staffing forecasts across a dozen people, permissions, accounting sync, and a mobile timer that your team will actually use. Build it if you are the only person who needs to see the numbers, buy it the moment payroll depends on them.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you define clients, projects with hourly rates and budgets, log time entries against them, and generate an invoice plus a margin report per project.
requirements: Node 20+ and a local machine or small VPS
Somewhere to store the SQLite file with backups
Manual export to your accountant, or a Stripe key if you want payment links
whatYouLose: Resource scheduling and utilization forecasting across a real team
Accounting integrations (QuickBooks, Xero) and clean tax handling
Native mobile and desktop timers, so time gets logged from memory instead of live
Roles and permissions, so you cannot let contractors see only their own hours
Reporting that stakeholders trust without you explaining the query
moatNotes: The lock-in is accounting sync plus years of historical hours and margins; nobody re-keys that into a homemade app.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the moment more than one person logs time, the software stops being a tracker and becomes the source of truth for invoicing and payroll. Agencies pay for the confidence that the number in the profitability report matches the number on the invoice matches the number in Xero, and for someone else to own that reconciliation. A solo operator has no such problem: they know what they worked on and what they charged. The bill scales with headcount for exactly the reason the value does.
notes: The single-user version of this is a weekend; the multi-seat version is an accounting product wearing a project management hat.
prompt:
Build a local-first agency operations app for a solo freelancer or two-person shop. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via Prisma, file at ./data/app.db
- Server actions for all mutations, no separate API layer
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, single user, no auth

Data model:
- Client: name, email, currency, default hourly rate, notes
- Project: client, name, status (active, paused, done), billing type (hourly or fixed fee), budget amount, budget hours, hourly rate override
- TimeEntry: project, date, minutes, description, billable flag, invoiced flag
- Expense: project, date, amount, description, billable flag
- Invoice: client, issue date, due date, line items derived from uncharged billable time and expenses, status (draft, sent, paid)

Features in scope:
- A running timer with start/stop that writes a TimeEntry, plus manual entry and inline editing on a week grid view
- Project detail page showing hours logged vs budget hours, cost vs budget amount, percent consumed, and a simple burn chart
- Invoice builder: pick a client, it pulls all uninvoiced billable time and expenses, lets you group lines by project or by description, edit amounts, then marks them invoiced
- Invoice render as a clean printable HTML page, print to PDF via the browser, no PDF library
- Profitability report: per project, revenue invoiced minus a configurable internal cost rate times hours, sorted by margin
- CSV export for time entries and invoices
- Seed script with two clients, three projects, and a month of plausible time entries

Out of scope, do not build:
multi-user roles, resource scheduling, accounting integrations, email sending, payment processing, mobile apps.

Keep any config in .env (CURRENCY, INTERNAL_COST_RATE, BUSINESS_NAME, BUSINESS_ADDRESS) with a .env.example committed. Write a README with setup, seed and backup instructions (just copy the SQLite file). Prefer dense tables over dashboards; this is a tool, not a demo.
